caption: What if Earth had no tilt? Our planet spins with its axis tilted about 23.4°, and that tilt, not our distance from the Sun, is what gives us seasons. Stand Earth perfectly straight and the seasons disappear. Every place on Earth would get roughly 12 hours of day and 12 hours of night, every single day of the year. Delhi would lose both its foggy Decembers and its scorching Mays and settle into one in-between season forever. At the poles, the Sun would sit on the horizon permanently, an endless sunrise. India's monsoon depends on summer heating of the land, so with no summer it could vanish as we know it. Plot twist: Earth is actually closest to the Sun in early January, in the middle of India's winter. On 3 January 2027 we'll be about 147.1 million km away, only around 3% closer than in July. Would YOU trade the seasons for one forever-season? 👇
